conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Fraud Division. This is Officer Mark Benson, badge number 582194. Whom am I speaking with today?
Hi, my name is Emily Watson. I got a voicemail to call this number about my taxes?
Yes, Emily, thank you for calling back. Before we proceed, can you confirm your full name and the last four digits of your Social Security number, so I can retrieve your IRS file?
Uh, sure. It's Emily Watson, and the last four are 3781.

Thank you, Emily. I have your case pulled up. There are several discrepancies in your federal tax filings from the last two years, and the IRS has initiated a case against you for tax evasion and fraud.
What? I don't understand. I just finished college and started working last year. I thought I did everything right.
According to our records, there are multiple errors, and a legal affidavit was issued this morning. A warrant for your arrest has also been processed. This is a very serious federal offense.
A warrant? Wait, Am I going to get arrested? Why didn't anyone tell me before?

We attempted to notify you by mail and phone, but you did not respond in time. The IRS does not take tax fraud lightly. If this is not resolved immediately, officers from your local police department will be dispatched to your address within the hour.
Oh my god, I had no idea. What am I supposed to do? I can't go to jail.

Emily, listen carefully. Since you have no prior offenses, you have a one-time opportunity to resolve this matter outside of court by making an immediate restitution payment to the IRS holding account.
I don't have a lot of money. How much do I owe? How do I pay?
Your total outstanding balance, including penalties, is $3,900. Payment must be made today to halt the legal action. Do you have access to your bank account or a credit card right now?
I have a debit card and some money in my checking account, but I don't think it's that much.

That will be sufficient to start. For your security, payments for IRS fraud cases are processed via Bitcoin to the IRS escrow wallet. Do you know how to use Bitcoin, or would you like step-by-step instructions?
I've never used Bitcoin before. I don't even have an account or anything.

That's not a problem. I will walk you through the process. First, you need to visit a nearby store such as CVS or Walgreens and purchase Bitcoin using a CoinFlip ATM or via a prepaid Bitcoin voucher. Are you able to get to a store within the next 30 minutes?
I think so. There's a CVS down the street from my apartment.
Excellent. Write down this wallet address: 3G9u8wKjzQ1TvZxJ1EbA5bqL2d6Z9wF4pQ. Once you purchase the Bitcoin, you will enter this address as the recipient. Do not share this code with anyone else.
Okay, I wrote it down. Do I just ask them for Bitcoin at the register?

You need to use the Bitcoin ATM inside the CVS. If you need assistance, I will stay on the line while you go. You will insert cash and send it directly to the wallet I provided. Do not hang up; otherwise, the warrant process will resume.
Alright, I'm leaving now. Should I call you when I get there?
Stay on the line, Emily. I need to verify payment in real time to stop the arrest order. Once you send the funds, I will confirm receipt and update your case file.
Okay. I'm really scared. Are you sure this will clear everything up?
As soon as the full payment is processed, your warrant will be revoked, and you'll receive an official clearance letter from the IRS. But you must not delay, or we cannot intervene further.
